newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Iddison Group reconsiders park plans.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Iddison Group reconsiders park plans.

text.p: New Zealand's Iddison Group Vietnam Ltd said in its annual report on Monday it was reconsidering its plans for the Saigon Water Park in Vietnam.

"It was originally anticipated that this project would be close to opening by now. However we have recently received a recommendation from the manager of the project to combine stages I and II which will result in increased costs," the company said in a release to shareholders.
"Although the manager has called on shareholders to contribute funds ahead of construction we have not agreed to any significant funding until a budget and a programme is settled," it said.

In regard to its aluminium extrusion business, Iddison said that following the recent purchase by Fletcher Aluminium of Comalco Carter Holt Harvey's aluminium extrusion business, extrusion orders to Vietnam were on the increase again.
"Fletcher has now offered us formal agreements relating to separate areas in the North and South of Vietnam and have effectively increased the royalty we receive," Iddison said.

It said the expanding construction industry in Vietnam was enabling it to proceed confidently with its concrete products joint venture, in which it has an effective 35 percent interest with Pendleton Corporation (35 percent), a firm of Wellington construction engineers. Vietnamese partners hold 30 percent.
